pages.basis: plain Paged.js measurement (3 pages) of justified, hyphenated German prose

expectedExit.derivation: All planted defects are warn rules (type/straight-quotes, type/spaced-hyphen, artifact/local-uri); no error-rule defect; the error rules measure every candidate.
expectedExit.environmentNote: Exit 4 with exitReason evidence/required-page-binding-incomplete is an environment failure (evidence binding not supported by the renderer), not an outcome of these documents; run the gate where the live path binds evidence (CI).

fontDependence: Only generic families (serif, sans-serif, monospace) are used. Line breaks, paragraph heights and therefore the position of flowing text depend on the fonts the renderer resolves; every construction fact below is built from explicit heights, fixed line pitches, forced breaks or SVG coordinates so that it does not depend on them, and every font-dependent outcome is listed as allowed.
features: planted file: URI and absolute path in links
clean counterparts: typographic quotes, en dashes, inch mark after a digit, code and kbd, digit ranges, single-letter formula, lang=en span, path in visible text

mustNotFire.why: running element: Paged.js clones it into a page margin box on every page (position: running). Under the release-semantics rule (README 'Release semantics', manifest.json releaseSemantics) content in margin boxes is not in the flow and is not measured by any rule, so no finding may name the element or any of its copies.
mustNotFire.docsBasis: README 'Release semantics'; docs/limitations.md 0.6.0 already says 'Blocks carrying the same source id are not always fragments of one flow'.

allowed.why: where a block splits and how many lines each fragment carries depends on font metrics and on Chromium's own widows/orphans handling inside the Paged.js fragmentainer

expectedDeclines.docsBasis: docs/rules/layout-orphan.md 'Skipped after a forced outgoing break'; the widow rule declines after a forced incoming break (declines list in the rule registry).

https URL

the path /srv/intranet/vorlagen/datenschutz appears only as visible text, not in a URI-bearing attribute (docs/rules/artifact-local-uri.md reads uriRefs). This entry can never match: under the README's id semantics for artifact/local-uri an id target matches only the URI-bearing attributes of the element and its descendants, and there are none here. It documents the control; a tool that reports the visible-text path is caught by the closed-world check, because no mustFire or allowed entry covers it.
